newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. investor group eyes Israel banking sector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investor group eyes Israel banking sector.

text.p: The former president of Republic New York Corp, Jeffrey Keil, has expressed interest in investing in Israel's banking sector, the official in charge of bank privatisation said.

Meir Jacobson, managing director of M.I. Holdings, the state company in charge of selling the government's banking shares, would not confirm or deny a report in the Maariv daily that he had met Keil last week to discuss a possible bid for Bank Hapoalim.
In September, Treasury director-general David Brodett said Keil had expressed interest in bidding for a controlling stake in Hapoalim, Israel's biggest bank.
Keil had announced in June he would leave his post at Republic to form his own investment partnership.
Maariv said a Keil-led group would participate in a consortium organised by Israeli businessman Eliezer Fishman which includes Bear Stearns.

The Fishman group is the only party bidding for a stake in Hapoalim after a second group headed by Claridge Israel dropped out in August. Claridge is the local investment arm of Canadian businessman Charles Bronfman.
Maariv said the Lazard Freres & Co investment bank was also part of the Keil group.
